researched_by: Claude (lexflow agent), read-only research; discovery list for the glass_studio_* process files, not a verified answer set
method: Every request used the User-Agent lexflow-research/0.1 (https://github.com/alibama/lexflow), obeyed robots.txt, and waited at least 1.5 s per host and 5 s between requests to web.archive.org. www.albemarle.org (Granicus behind Akamai) and serviceauthority.org answer 403 to automated clients, so their pages and PDFs were read from the newest Internet Archive capture found through the Wayback availability API; the capture URL is recorded for each page. abc.virginia.gov and deq.virginia.gov also refuse automated clients and their newest captures are from 2023 and 2011, so their statements rest on the Code of Virginia and the Virginia Administrative Code (law.lis.virginia.gov, read live). vdh.virginia.gov (Blue Ridge Health District), law.lis.virginia.gov, columbiagasva.com and dominionenergy.com were read live. Municode (County Code, including Chapter 18 Zoning Ordinance and Chapter 17 Water Protection Ordinance) was not fetched because its terms forbid automated access and republication; sections are cited by number only. No browser, forms, logins or submissions were used; the Civic Access portal, Fire Rescue web forms, ACSA service request and ABC licensing portal were not opened. Docker was down, so no quote was matched against the lexflow index; every quote in the process files is marked source: official-page.

Chapter 17 (Water Protection Ordinance) governs land disturbance. Chapter 8 (Licenses) is quoted from the 2019 ordinance on the County's Legistar API, as in bpol_business_license. website_terms.summary: albemarle.org allows browsing for informational purposes but forbids redistributing or reposting site content without written permission (see fixtures/places/va/discovery-albemarle.json). Every albemarle.org quote in the glass_studio_* files is short, is kept only as evidence, and carries a paraphrase for display.

key_findings: Front door: the free Monday pre-application meeting with Community Development (cdd-preapps@albemarle.org; request in Civic Access with a sketch plan by noon Monday), mandatory before a special use permit, exploratory for everything else.

Zoning: every commercial or industrial business needs a Zoning Clearance ($60 plus 4%) before a tenant up-fit building permit and before any sign permit; a new building needs an approved site development plan ($1,775 plus 4%); special use permits are $2,365 plus 4% plus a $235 notice fee; a Letter of Determination on use classification is $220 plus 4%; Rural Areas home occupations are capped at 25% of the dwelling or 1,500 sq. ft., 10 vehicle trips a day, two employees, and exclude any use needing a special use permit and restaurants.

Building: Civic Access commercial permits (new commercial $0.24 per sq. ft. up to 5,000 then $0.17; alterations $0.20 per sq. ft.; mechanical $0.04 per sq. ft.; gas lines $40; change of occupancy $175; temporary CO $150 per 30 days; 4% surcharge); life-safety plan required; each trade files its own sub-permit; CO within five working days of the final inspection.

Fire: Albemarle enforces the SFPC; its 2022 Fire Marshal fee schedule requires operational permits for compressed gas (oxygen over 504 cu. ft.), hot work, LP-gas (any business storage), industrial ovens, places of assembly over 50 and open flames in dining areas, mostly $200 a year per location; facility inspection free for two hours then $100 an hour; re-inspection $100; appeals within 14 days to the local fire code board ($350).

Business license: Finance & Budget (no Commissioner of the Revenue); apply by email or mail; $0 under $25,000, $50 to $100,000, then $0.20 (retail) or $0.36 (services) per $100; manufacturers selling at wholesale at the place of manufacture are exempt by state law; BTPP or machinery and tools return by May 1 at $4.28 per $100 (25% of cost in year one).

Food and drink: Blue Ridge Health District plan review and permit before construction and 30 days before opening ($80 on the page; $40 plus $40 on the 2019 schedule), CO required first, pre-opening inspection with a certified food manager; County 6% food and beverage tax by the 20th monthly; ABC $195 application plus $450 (wine and beer) or $1,050 (mixed beverage, up to 100 seats) a year, or $40 banquet license per event; County ABC flat fee $37.50 to $500.

Utilities and environment: ACSA needs a signed building permit before a meter, charges system development and RWSA capacity fees, and requires a FOG device and permit for food service; well and septic through the Health District ($350 well, $525 septic); propane tank needs a $120 mechanical permit and the LP-gas fire permit; land disturbance over 10,000 sq. ft. needs a VESMP permit ($235 plus 4% under an acre, $2,205 plus 4% to five acres); gas-fired furnaces under 50,000,000 Btu per hour are exempt from DEQ minor NSR permits.

The County's BPOL and machinery-and-tools classification of a studio that makes, sells and teaches.
The current Blue Ridge Health District food permit fee ($80 on the June 2026 page versus $40 plus $40 on the 2019 schedule) and ACSA FOG permit fees.
Which ABC license fits a studio serving wine and beer at ticketed classes without being a full restaurant (abc.virginia.gov unreadable; 2023 capture only).
DEQ's view of a studio's furnace and colorants (deq.virginia.gov unreadable; 2011 and 2023 captures only).
ACSA connection charge amounts (table not read cleanly), natural gas availability by parcel, and the Water Protection Ordinance thresholds (Municode).
The 2027 Community Development fee schedule adopted April 22, 2026 (amounts not read).
